The Meelick Team Jig

I’ve just been looking at a webpage that says:

“Eddy was born in Meelick, Eyrecourt, near Ballinisloe, Co. Galway, in 1933. Lived in that area till 1958, moved to Castlerea, Co. Roscommon. Has 20 compositions. Plays both button and fiddle. His compositions often exhibit a strong East Galway influence. Respected traditional musician, tunes circulated through sessions, radio performances, and concerts.”

Meelick Team Jig commemorates a hurling team from his native parish which qualified for and played in the first All-Ireland Hurling Finals held in 1884."

Other titles include:

-Eddie Kelly’s Jig (P.J.Hernon), and also on a Liz Carroll recording (A Friend Indeed)

Martin Talty’s Jig (Clare Concertinas Bernard O’Sullivan and Tommy McMahon)

On Mary MacNamara’s recent CD it was played in D minor, using a C/F Anglo concertina. In Bulmer and Sharpley (1975) it was given the title McGreevy’s

↳ Posted by Dr. Dow on March 14th, 2003.

“Martin Talty’s Jig” ~ Bernard O’Sullivan & Tommy McMahon: Clare Concertinas"

Tommy McMahon’s take on this, on concertina, I’ve left out his octave drops, where he plays the occasional note down an octave from the usual, meaning what most instruments would tend to do. However, I quite like those hiccups and am a long time fan of his playing, and Bernard O’Sullivan’s too. ;-)

↳ Posted by ceolachan on September 4th, 2012.

Listed in Bulmer & Sharpley

This tune is in Bulmer & Sharpley’s “Music from Ireland” volume IV, number 57 as “McGreavy’s.”

I recorded it on my 1998 CD “’Til Time Is No More” in a set with “Caterpillar” and “Willie Coleman’s.”
